newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has cancelled an upcoming trip to the United States in order to deal with controversial domestic legislation, his spokesman said on Saturday.

"Yes, that's true...He was to have left on June 21," spokesman Ofir Akunis told Reuters when asked if the trip had been cancelled due to the pending legislation on who may perform conversions to Judaism. He said Netanyahu was to have gone to New York to attend U.N. functions.

Akunis refused to comment on Israeli media reports the cancellation was due to the deadlock in Middle East peace moves. A second Netanyahu aide, Shai Bazak, later denied those reports, saying: "That's not correct."

Israel's army radio said Netanyahu had cancelled the trip because he had hoped to fit in a meeting with President Bill Clinton but now wanted to avoid talks with Clinton due to the faltering peace process.
"That (domestic legislation) is the official excuse...The problem is that the diplomatic process is deadlocked and strongly deadlocked," the radio's diplomatic reporter Udi Segal said.
"He (Netanyahu) thought he would arrive...after a summit, after some sort of meeting with Arafat," Segal said.

On Thursday, Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz shuttled between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in his latest bid to solve a deep crisis caused when Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

He returned to Egypt saying more work was needed to end the impasse. Palestinians demand Israel halt settlement construction before they will resume substantive negotiations. Netanyahu vows to continue building.
